subject: Biology
title: Hormones of Heart, Kidney, & Gastrointestinal Tract
learningObjectives: Explain the vasodilatory and natriuretic actions of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF)
Describe renal Juxtaglomerular (JG) cell secretion of Erythropoietin (EPO) and Calcitriol
Detail gastrointestinal regulatory peptides: Gastrin, Secretin, CCK-PZ, and GIP
content:
### 9.1 Hormones Secreted by Non-Endocrine Organs

1. **Heart (Atrial Wall)**:
   - **Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF)**: A 28-amino acid peptide hormone released by atrial cardiomyocytes in response to high atrial stretch (elevated blood volume/venous return).
   - **Mechanism**: Promotes systemic vasodilation, relaxes vascular smooth muscle, inhibits Renin and Aldosterone release, and increases renal sodium and water excretion (**Natriuresis**), effectively lowering systemic blood pressure.
2. **Kidneys (Juxtaglomerular Apparatus)**:
   - **Erythropoietin (EPO)**: Glycoprotein hormone secreted by interstitial peritubular/JG cells in response to tissue hypoxia. Stimulates proliferation and differentiation of proerythroblasts in bone marrow, accelerating **Erythropoiesis**.
   - **Calcitriol ($1,25\text{-(OH)}_2\text{D}_3$)**: Active steroid hormone form of Vitamin D produced via $1\alpha$-hydroxylase activation in proximal tubular cells, enhancing active intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption.
3. **Gastrointestinal Tract**:
   - **Gastrin**: Secreted by G-cells in the gastric pyloric antrum; stimulates parietal cells to secrete hydrochloric acid ($\text{HCl}$) and chief cells to secrete pepsinogen.
   - **Secretin**: Secreted by S-cells in the duodenum in response to acidic chyme ($\text{pH} < 4.5$); stimulates the exocrine pancreas to secrete watery, bicarbonate-rich fluid to neutralize acid.
   - **Cholecystokinin (CCK / CCK-PZ)**: Secreted by I-cells in the duodenum and jejunum in response to amino acids and fatty acids; stimulates gall bladder contraction (discharging bile) and pancreatic acinar secretion of digestive enzymes.
   - **Gastric Inhibitory Peptide (GIP / Glucose-Dependent Insulinotropic Peptide)**: Secreted by K-cells in the duodenum; inhibits gastric acid secretion and motility while augmenting glucose-stimulated insulin release.

conceptBreakdown.heading: ANF vs RAAS Antagonism
conceptBreakdown.explanation: ANF serves as the body's natural physiological antagonist to the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS), preventing hypervolemia and severe arterial hypertension.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Incretin Effect of GIP & GLP-1
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Oral glucose ingestion produces a significantly larger insulin spike than intravenous glucose infusion due to the rapid release of gut incretin hormones (GIP and GLP-1) from enteroendocrine cells.
